news.title: £250m to be invested in grassroots across Greater Manchester ahead of 2035 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Following the news that the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is coming to the UK, with our region firmly frontrunners to host games from the get-go, a major investment of more than £250 million into grassroots football across Greater Manchester has also been announced. Revealed by the Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig, the huge injection of funds into various football facilities is not only to support the region’s ability to host fixtures but also to further cement this particularly passionate part of the country as ‘the home of football’. For lots of us, that was settled from birth, but getting behind grassroots with initiatives like this certainly helps reinforce that argument. Celebrating the influx of funding over the next few years, the Mayor outlined more details on how this money is going to be spent via an official announcement on social media:.

news.title: Ghana’s Black Challenge return home with historic World Cup trophy on Thursday
news.lede: Ghana's Black Challenge are expected to return to Accra on Thursday, 26 November, with the country's first Amputee Football World Cup trophy after defeating Morocco in the final in Mexico. The National Paralympic Committee of Ghana (NPC Ghana) has confirmed the team's arrival following their historic 1-0 victory over Morocco in Sunday's final in San Juan de los Lagos. Captain Richard Arthur Opentil scored the decisive goal to secure the championship, bringing an end to Ghana's campaign with a landmark achievement in the competition. The Black Challenge will be welcomed home after becoming the first Ghanaian side to win the Amputee Football World Cup, adding another major achievement to the country's para sports history.

news.title: Kofi Adams announces $10,000 reward for every Black Challenge player after historic World Cup win
news.lede: Ghana’s Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Adams has announced an additional US$10,000 reward for each member of the Black Challenge following their historic success at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The announcement comes after Ghana secured their maiden world title with a narrow 1-0 victory over Morocco in Sunday's final. An own goal in the second half proved decisive as the Black Challenge completed their campaign with the championship trophy, marking a significant achievement for the country. Adams, who is also the Member of Parliament for Buem, made the announcement during a virtual engagement with the players through Zoom.

news.title: Nigeria Not Ready to Host World Cup, Infantino
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino says Nigeria is not currently ready to host the senior FIFA World Cup, pointing to gaps in stadium infrastructure, airports, hotels and transportation networks. However, he believes the country has the resources, football passion and potential to work towards hosting the competition in the future. Infantino made the remarks during an exclusive interview with ARISE News in Abuja on Monday, November 23, when asked whether Nigeria could host a tournament of the World Cup's magnitude. The FIFA president explained that hosting the World Cup requires more than a strong football culture.

news.title: Ghana makes history as Black Challenge win 2026 Amputee Football World Cup
news.lede: GHANA'S Black Challenge have etched their names into football history after being crowned 2026 Amputee Football World Cup champions, following a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Morocco in Sunday's final in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. Captain Richard Opentil emerged as Ghana's hero, scoring the decisive goal in the 32nd minute to secure a historic triumph and deliver the country's first-ever world title in amputee football. In a fiercely contested encounter between two of Africa's finest sides, the Black Challenge demonstrated remarkable determination, resilience and defensive discipline to protect their slender advantage and hold off Morocco until the final whistle. The encounter served as a rematch of the 2024 African Amputee Cup of Nations final and the 2023 African Para Games final.

news.title: Southampton snubbed as potential host city for 2035 football Women's World Cup
news.lede: SOUTHAMPTON has been snubbed as a potential host city for the 2035 Women's World Cup, which will be hosted in the UK. FIFA confirmed on Monday that England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will jointly host the tournament — the first World Cup staged in England since the men's triumph in 1966. The plan calls for 19 venues: 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales. However, St Mary's is not among the 22 provisional stadiums, with the final list due to contain 14 to 16 grounds.

news.title: Scoring a Goal for Free Knowledge: How WikiSport’s Football Project Transformed Uzbek Football Coverage on Wikipedia
news.lede: In Uzbekistan, football isn’t just a pastime–it’s a national obsession. Yet for years, fans searching for reliable, structured information in Uzbek about their own domestic leagues, historic clubs, or local players often hit a dead end. Articles on the Uzbek Wikipedia were either missing entirely or consisted of little more than a single stub sentence. Launched as a specialized thematic track under the broader WikiStipendiya marathon, the WikiSport: Football project set out to change that.

news.title: What the 2035 Women’s World Cup means for local girls’ football
news.lede: With confirmation that the UK will host the 2035 Women's World Cup, it feels like another proper milestone for the women's and girls' game across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland—and plenty to look forward to even from right here in North Herts. We all saw what happened after the Euros: more girls kicking a ball in parks and on rec pitches, bigger crowds, and a real shift in how the game is treated. Having a home World Cup on the calendar for 2035—with matches proposed just down the line in London and across the UK—gives the next generation something real to aim for, much like 1966 did for plenty of us growing up. Of course, not everyone is on board.
